## Design

### 2026-10-06 – I started by creating the files of my project, then I opened the schematic editor but it froze cause my PC is bad. I went on slack for a while to research then I edited the schematic sheet data and en

**3h**

I started by creating the files of my project, then I opened the schematic editor but it froze cause my PC is bad. I went on slack for a while to research then I edited the schematic sheet data and entered my project info, after that I opened the tutorial page and started following it. The tutorial had provided their own symbols, which I tried to import but couldn't, then I went on youtube to find a tutorial and found one. After that I successfully(took a few mins) imported the symbol in my schematic editor then start by adding ESP32 C3 microcontroller, I didn't know how to block a pin so, I googled it, blocked the pins and after that I added the button symbols, took a few tries cause it was crashing, and after that I added a OLED screen and at last I arranged all the schematics.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/43eafa3d-5137-4e1c-9535-d2d97ccbf592/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-08 – First of all, I opened my project and added an RGB light symbol to my schematic, arranging it with all the other symbols. I went to the tutorial page to see how  to assign symbols to footprints, then

**2h**

First of all, I opened my project and added an RGB light symbol to my schematic, arranging it with all the other symbols. I went to the tutorial page to see how  to assign symbols to footprints, then opened the footprint assigning tool but, I couldn't find the imported symbols there. After searching KiCad a little bit, I found the footprint editor and remembered that I had imported the symbols, but not the footprints.

I imported the footprints and restarted the footprint assignment tool. Then I noticed that my resistor wasn't labeled * 10k * as shown in the tutorial page. I researched how to change the value, and it turns out I just had to double-click and change the value. I did that and started the footprint assignment tool again.

This time, I assigned all the symbols to their respective footprints, including the RGB light I added on my own. Finally, I opened the board editor, but the footprints weren't loading. I will fix it tomorrow.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/08dab700-1d0b-4316-9f0b-ef5bc7694057/video.mp4)
